item.title: See your page the way Googlebot does.
item.description:
30-second trick: See your page the way Googlebot does.
Search Console's URL Inspection tool can fetch a live page as Google and show the rendered HTML, a screenshot, and the resources it could not load.
Try it now: Search the rendered HTML for your main heading and your key facts. If they are missing there, Google may not see them either.
How a public-page review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=evergreen-2026-11&utm_content=googlebot

item.title: Myth: a sitemap gets every page indexed.
item.description:
Myth vs fact: Myth: a sitemap gets every page indexed.
A sitemap helps search engines discover your pages. Google says plainly that it does not guarantee every listed page will be crawled and indexed.
Check it: Open the Pages report in Search Console and filter it by your sitemap. Each page left out is listed with its reason.
How a public-page review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=evergreen-2026-11&utm_content=myth-sitemap

item.title: SRI: a fingerprint for borrowed scripts.
item.description:
Word of the day: SRI: a fingerprint for borrowed scripts.
Subresource Integrity puts a hash of the file in the tag. If the CDN ever serves anything else, the browser refuses to run it.
Spot it: List the scripts you load from other domains. Add an integrity hash to every one that has a fixed version.
How a public-page review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=evergreen-2026-11&utm_content=sri
#WebSecurity #Programming #Phishing #QA #SRI #QAlab

item.title: Myth: one line of code makes a site accessible.
item.description:
Myth vs fact: Myth: one line of code makes a site accessible.
Overlay widgets promise WCAG compliance from a single script. In April 2025 the US Federal Trade Commission ordered one vendor to pay $1 million and stop claiming its tool makes any site compliant without evidence.
Check it: Spend the overlay budget on your shared templates first: header, navigation, forms and footer.
How a public-page review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=evergreen-2026-11&utm_content=myth-overlay

item.title: Bancolombia's site won't let you zoom.
item.description:
Language versions link to each other, share cards are complete, and pages read without JavaScript. But the viewport sets maximum-scale=1, which blocks pinch-zoom on many phones for people who need larger text.
The lesson for every team: Drop maximum-scale and user-scalable=no from your viewport tag. Zoom is how many people read.

item.description:
